analysis_scope.sampling_notes: The checkout is shallow with depth 50, so history before the available commits may be truncated; only three commits are visible. All substantive first-party source was inspected. stated_purpose: A Python day-trading research tool that fetches Yahoo Finance market data, calculates SMA, MACD, and RSI indicators, generates rule-based signals, and optionally backtests them.

observed_capabilities.statement: The command-line application accepts ticker, interval, period, strategy, trend-mode, output, and backtest parameters.
The data layer fetches adjusted OHLCV bars through yfinance, converts timestamps to New York time, optionally filters regular market hours, and validates bar count and price consistency.
The indicator and signal layers calculate SMA 20/50/200, MACD 12/26/9, and RSI 14, then produce BUY, SELL, or HOLD decisions using pullback or stacked trend rules.
Three presets are implemented: current requires all three indicator conditions, aggressive requires any two, and conservative adds stronger trend confirmation and a volume filter.
The application can export individual and combined signal CSVs, compare strategies, run a next-bar-open backtest with commission and slippage inputs, and generate an Excel workbook.

architecture.statement: main.py orchestrates a sequential pipeline from Yahoo Finance retrieval through validation, indicator calculation, warm-up removal, signal generation, CSV export, optional backtesting, and multi-strategy comparison.
Strategy behavior is represented by dataclass configurations selected through a StrategyType enum and consumed by the shared signal-generation functions.

The system is a local batch-oriented research application rather than a live trading service: it has no broker integration, persistent application datastore, web interface, scheduler, or deployment configuration.

accomplishments.statement: A recorded September 2025 run processed 1,620 SPY bars, retained 1,420 after warm-up, executed all three strategies with backtesting, and completed in 10.5 seconds.
Tracked outputs include six signal CSVs, an Excel report, and an execution log, providing evidence that the primary research workflow produced tangible results.
Signal logic uses prior-bar values for MACD and RSI crossovers, while the backtest executes a signal using the following bar's open price to reduce direct lookahead bias.

gaps.statement: There are no first-party automated tests or CI workflows to verify indicator calculations, strategy conditions, exports, or backtest accounting.
The dependency manifest omits openpyxl even though the Excel report generator imports it, and the README does not document the later multi-strategy and Excel-report additions.
The backtester operates in fixed one-unit positions and lacks position sizing, stops, take-profit rules, exposure controls, benchmark comparison, and rigorous intraday annualization.
The Excel report embeds fixed SPY execution details and performance figures rather than deriving its summary entirely from the selected input files.
No live brokerage execution capability is implemented despite the repository's trading theme.

risks.statement: The repository tracks a complete platform-specific virtual environment, compiled binaries, bytecode, bootstrap scripts, generated market data, reports, and logs; this inflates the repository and creates portability, provenance, and dependency-maintenance risk.
The recorded positive result for the current strategy is based on only three buy signals over one 60-day SPY sample, so it is not strong evidence of general strategy performance.
The absence of tests makes financial metric and signal regressions difficult to detect, particularly as recent changes expanded the strategy logic substantially.
The repository has had no visible commit activity since September 2025 and has no open issues or pull requests, suggesting the implementation is dormant.

suggested_next_actions.statement: Remove the tracked virtual environment, bytecode, generated outputs, and bootstrap installers from version control; expand .gitignore and recreate dependencies from a complete pinned manifest.
Add deterministic unit tests for indicators, crossover boundaries, all strategy presets, next-bar execution, commissions, drawdown, and export schemas before relying on further performance results.
Make the Excel summary derive from actual result files and document the multi-strategy workflow and openpyxl dependency.
If the project is revived, evaluate strategies over multiple symbols, regimes, and out-of-sample periods with realistic sizing and transaction-cost assumptions.

questions: Was this intended to remain an educational research tool, or was live or paper-trading integration planned?
Are the generated SPY datasets and reports meant to be durable reference fixtures or disposable run outputs?
Should the repository be revived with validation work, retained as a historical experiment, or archived?
What position-sizing and risk-management assumptions should a credible backtest use?

evidence.summary: Public repository on main with no description, no open issues or pull requests, and last recorded push on 2025-09-09.
Documents a Yahoo Finance SMA/MACD/RSI signal generator, command-line usage, trading rules, CSV output, optional backtesting, and an educational-use disclaimer.

Contains nine first-party implementation modules, generated outputs, installer scripts, bytecode, and a tracked virtual environment comprising 8,032 of 8,062 tracked files; no first-party tests, CI, notebooks, or deployment artifacts were found.
Lists yfinance, pandas, numpy, pytz, and argparse, but not openpyxl used by the report generator.
Contains only the entry 'venv', which does not exclude the tracked trading_env directory or generated artifacts.
Implements the CLI and orchestrates data retrieval, validation, indicators, strategies, exports, comparisons, and optional backtests.
Fetches yfinance OHLCV history, normalizes timezone, filters market hours, drops missing rows, and validates price-bar quality.
Implements SMA, EMA/MACD, Wilder or simple RSI, and warm-up removal.
Implements trend filters, MACD and RSI crossovers, volume confirmation, three signal-combination modes, and signal validation.
Defines current, aggressive, and conservative strategy configurations using an enum and dataclass.
Implements a one-position, fixed-unit backtester using next-bar-open execution, flat commissions, proportional slippage, trade logs, an equity curve, and summary metrics.
Validates, orders, rounds, names, and writes signal datasets to CSV.
Combines strategy-specific signals and produces CSV comparison tables from signal and optional backtest results.
Builds a styled multi-sheet Excel workbook from recent CSVs but includes hard-coded strategy summary and execution values.

Records a completed all-strategy SPY 15-minute run over 1,420 post-warm-up bars: current produced 3 buys and a reported 0.24% return, aggressive produced 63 signals and -0.07%, and conservative produced no signals.
A tracked 1,420-row combined export contains OHLCV data, indicators, condition flags, and signals for all three strategies; related individual CSVs and an Excel workbook are also tracked.
The shallow checkout exposes three commits dated 2025-09-01 through 2025-09-09; the final commit expanded strategies and added comparison, report, logs, datasets, and installer artifacts.

confidence.rationale: All first-party implementation and available history were inspected, and a recorded successful run plus generated outputs support the primary workflow. Confidence is limited by the shallow history, lack of automated tests or CI, inability to rerun the network-dependent workflow, and weak performance-validation evidence.

limitations: The repository was analyzed read-only, so no files were modified and no network-dependent trading run was performed.
The clone is shallow at depth 50, and only three commits are available for historical analysis.
Vendored virtual-environment package source was not inspected individually because it is generated third-party content.
The supplied GitHub snapshot reports no open issues or pull requests, but no broader branch or historical issue analysis was available.
Generated performance figures were treated as recorded artifacts, not independently reproduced or validated investment results.
